summary.headline: A recovering packaging maker with a much better 2026, but at Rs 16.30 the price is about 8% above fair value, and the business tests aren't passed yet
summary.text:
J.F. Packaging PLC (JFP.N0000), 70% owned by Lankem Ceylon, makes flexible packaging, adhesive tapes and paper tubes, PET bottles and injection-moulded products. It listed in November 2025, raising Rs 600mn at Rs 11.60 to repay loans. Profit has jumped: Rs 246mn in April–September 2026 against Rs 74mn a year earlier, on 26% higher sales and a gross margin of 31% (24.5%).

Fair value is about **Rs 15.13** (buy below **Rs 12.86**, strong buy below **Rs 11.35**). The share trades at about 7.4 times twelve-month earnings, which already prices in most of the improvement. Debt is still high (net debt Rs 1.73bn, almost equal to equity) and rose again in the half, so value is very sensitive to whether the new margins last.

Only 2 of the 4 business tests pass (debt and cash). Return on equity was 9–12% in the three years before the IPO, and profit has swung from break-even to Rs 911mn and back. Category 3: avoid for now. Watch for two or three more quarters at 20%+ ROE before buying.

quality.reason: Debt is just inside the limit and cash flow covers profit, but returns were low until this year and the profit record is far from steady.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
tests.note: Company ROE 9% (2023/24), 12% (2024/25) and 12% (2025/26) (p. 151). Twelve months to Sep 2026: 24% (profit Rs 0.362bn over average equity), helped by lower debt costs and a 31% gross margin, and flattered by pre-IPO equity in the average. One strong half isn't yet a record; would pass if 2026/27 holds about 20%.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: No loss in five years, but profit was Rs 0.3mn in 2021/22 (equity was negative), Rs 911mn in 2022/23, then Rs 72mn, Rs 131mn and Rs 190mn (p. 151). Too uneven to call steady.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: Operating cash flow (after interest and tax) Rs 0.212bn + Rs 0.174bn in 2024/25–2025/26 against profit Rs 0.131bn + Rs 0.190bn. But after capex (Rs 0.23–0.25bn a year) and lease payments, free cash was negative both years, so the Rs 86mn dividends were in effect paid from the IPO and borrowing; April–September 2026 operating cash Rs 0.141bn against profit Rs 0.246bn as stock rose.

modelsNote: Four methods are averaged in each scenario: a whole-company DCF plus the tea-plantation shares, P/E, justified price to book and residual income. No dividend model: the company has paid two dividends since listing and hasn't stated a policy. Growth check: the base case's 9% and bull's 11% compare with 9.9% supported by 2025/26 reinvestment (98% of after-tax operating profit) at a 10.1% return on capital; bull was cut from 13%. Maintenance capex: no company split, so bear treats all capex as maintenance (Rs 0.24bn) and base/bull use depreciation (Rs 0.13bn); 2025/26 capex was about half growth (new machinery at Kiffs and Alliance Five). Ratio notes: the 40.7% tax rate of 2025/26 is above normal because of withholding tax on subsidiary dividends and deferred tax; the DCF uses 33.9% from the latest half. Dividends were more than cash after maintenance capex in 2025/26 (cover 0.5×): flagged as at risk.

scenarios.common: Required return from CAPM with a country premium: risk-free 8.24% (12.24% bond less 4.0% default spread), mature premium 4.2% plus country premium 6.08%, beta 0.83. Weights bear 30 / base 50 / bull 20. Net debt Rs 1.728bn and NAV Rs 10.48 at 30 Sep 2026; 172.13mn shares.

buyPlan.realism: The buy price Rs 12.86 is 21% below Rs 16.30. The share hit Rs 12.50 in December 2025 and traded Rs 14.00–17.30 in July–September 2026, so the first tier is near the recent range and Rs 12.86 needs a market dip; Rs 11.35 is below the Rs 11.60 IPO price.

higher: Two or three more quarters with a gross margin near 30% and ROE above 20%, which would pass the returns test.
Borrowings falling back below Rs 1.5bn as stock is run down, cutting interest.
A stated dividend policy covered by free cash.

Debt rising further to fund stock or machinery.
Price wars in flexible packaging and PET bottles (the report names both).
Rules on single-use plastics hurting demand.

fullText:
**J.F. Packaging PLC (JFP.N0000): first analysis, 23 November 2026**

**Summary.** A packaging maker whose profits have jumped since its November 2025 listing, at a price that already reflects most of that. Fair value is about **Rs 15.13**, buy price **Rs 12.86**, strong buy **Rs 11.35**, against Rs 16.30 (last trade, 30 September 2026). Only 2 of the 4 business tests pass, so the category is **3: avoid for now**. The case to buy later is that the new margins last and return on equity stays near 20%. The risk is that debt is still almost equal to equity and is rising again.

**The business.** Lankem Ceylon PLC owns 69.95%. The group has four parts: flexible packaging (the listed company itself, about half of revenue), Ceylon Tapes (adhesive tapes, plus a paper canister and tube business bought from Iceman as an asset buy-out in 2025), Kiffs (PET bottles, jars and lids) and Alliance Five (injection-moulded thread cones and coir products, all exported). Almost all sales are in Sri Lanka, to FMCG, apparel, tea and other exporters. Revenue outside Sri Lanka was Rs 97mn in 2025/26, but the report says much more is sold to exporters.

**The IPO.** In October 2025 the company sold 51.7mn new shares at Rs 11.60 (Rs 600mn), 6.3 times oversubscribed, and listed on 19 November 2025. All the money repaid term loans and Bank of Ceylon import loans (p. 149). There are now 172.13mn shares.

**Results.**

| | 2023/24 | 2024/25 | 2025/26 | Apr–Sep 2025 | Apr–Sep 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue, Rs bn | 3.79 | 4.39 | 4.50 | 2.13 | 2.68 |
| Gross margin | 27% | 26% | 26% | 24.5% | 31.2% |
| Operating profit, Rs mn | 566 | 608 | 524 | 233 | 487 |
| Profit after tax, Rs mn | 72 | 131 | 190 | 74 | 246 |
| EPS, Rs | 0.60 | 1.08 | 1.37 | 0.61 | 1.43 |

The 2025/26 operating profit includes Rs 36mn of one-off IPO costs. The 2025/26 tax charge (41% of profit before tax) includes withholding tax on subsidiaries' dividends and deferred tax. Earlier years were very uneven: profit was Rs 0.3mn in 2021/22, when equity was negative, and Rs 911mn in 2022/23. In April–September 2026, packaging's profit before tax rose to Rs 243mn from Rs 21mn, on new customers, fuller capacity and better mix. The September quarter (Rs 104mn) was below the June quarter (Rs 143mn).

**Balance sheet.** At 30 September 2026, borrowings, leases and overdraft were Rs 1.86bn, cash Rs 0.14bn, so net debt was Rs 1.73bn against equity of Rs 1.80bn (0.96×). Inventories rose Rs 362mn in the half, and the company borrowed Rs 354mn of new long-term loans. The interim doesn't show lease liabilities separately, so they are counted inside borrowings. The group also holds Rs 319mn of unquoted shares in Consolidated Tea Plantations (Rs 1.85 a share) and Rs 211mn of goodwill.

**Required return.** The beta is 0.83: Damodaran's global packaging unlevered beta (0.58) relevered for JFP's debt. It is provisional, because his emerging-markets file couldn't be opened and the share has no 5-year trading history. Cost of equity is 8.24% + 0.83 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 16.8% (bear 18.3%, bull 15.3%). Debt is 38% of the company's value at a 10.8% cost before tax, so WACC is 12.8% (13.8% / 11.9%).

**Methods (Rs a share).**

| Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole-company DCF + investments | 3.39 | 21.76 | 35.05 | 18.91 |
| P/E | 10.99 | 15.30 | 21.12 | 15.17 |
| Justified P/B | 7.33 | 11.55 | 16.90 | 11.35 |
| Residual income | 8.77 | 15.01 | 24.78 | 15.09 |
| Average | 7.62 | 15.90 | 24.46 | **15.13** |

- **DCF**: starts from twelve-month operating profit to September 2026 (Rs 0.78bn, plus the IPO costs added back), taxed at 33.9%. The bear case is 15% lower in case the gross margin falls back. Growth is 4% / 9% / 11% for five years, then 4% / 5% / 6%. Because debt is large, the equity value swings from Rs 3 to Rs 35. About 81% of the base value and 86% of the bull value come after year 5.
- **P/E**: EPS to March 2027 of Rs 2.20 / 2.50 / 2.75 (Rs 1.43 already earned; run-rate Rs 2.40), at justified P/Es of 5.0 / 6.1 / 7.7.
- **P/B and residual income**: book Rs 10.48, with ROE settling at 14% / 18% / 21% from today's 24%.
- **Growth check**: 2025/26 reinvestment (98% of after-tax operating profit, mostly capex and working capital) at a 10.1% return on capital supports 9.9% growth. Base (9%) and bull (11%, cut from 13%) are within the limit.
- **Maintenance capex**: the company gives no split. About half of the Rs 248mn spent in 2025/26 was above depreciation (Rs 131mn), going on new machinery at Kiffs and Alliance Five. So the high capex is mostly growth, judged on its return.
- **Dividends**: Rs 86mn was paid in March 2026 and again in September 2026, about a quarter of profit. Cash after maintenance capex covered it only 0.5× in 2025/26, so the dividend is at risk if margins fall.

**Business tests (2 of 4).** Debt: pass, but only just (0.96×). Cash: pass, since operating cash covered profit 1.2× over two years, though free cash after capex was negative. Returns: fail, with ROE 9–12% in the three years before the IPO and 24% only over the latest twelve months. Steady profit: fail, given the swings above.

**Buy plan (500 shares).** 200 at up to Rs 15.13, 150 at up to Rs 12.86, 150 at up to Rs 11.35: about Rs 6,658, an average of Rs 13.32. The share traded Rs 14.00–17.30 in July–September 2026 and fell to Rs 12.50 in December 2025, so the buy price needs a market dip. Wait for the business tests to improve before starting.

**Management.** Management promises capacity expansion, more paper and recyclable packaging, exports and possibly acquisitions, but names no amounts. Profit and capacity are on track. The stronger balance sheet is not: debt rose again within six months.

**What would change the view.** Higher: two or three more quarters at a 30% gross margin and 20%+ ROE, debt falling, a stated dividend policy. Lower: polymer costs or the rupee squeezing margins, more borrowing, price wars, or plastic rules.

**Uncertain.** The price is the 30 September 2026 last trade, because the CSE site couldn't be reached. The September 2026 dividend's per-share amount isn't printed. The beta is a global stand-in. Per-share figures for 2021/22 and 2022/23 were printed before a share sub-division and aren't comparable.
